newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean prosecutors summon minister, MP over Hanbo.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean prosecutors summon minister, MP over Hanbo.

text.p: South Korean state prosecutors on Wednesday summoned for questioning Home Affairs Minister Kim Woo-suk and another leading ruling party member of parliament over a loan scandal, a prosecution official said.
The lawmaker is Hwang Byung-tai, a former ambassador to China, he said.

On Tuesday, prosecutors probing huge loans to the failed Hanbo Steel Co arrested two ruling party lawmakers, one of them the highest ranking New Korea Party official after President Kim Young-sam and the party chairman.

Chung Tae-soo, founder of the Hanbo Group has already been arrested on charges of fraud and other violations in connection with five trillion won ($5.8 billion) in loans its steelmaking flagship piled up before it was declared insolvent on January 23.
Two bankers have also been arrested on bribery charges.
Political analysts said the scandal, which has rocked the country, appeared set to hit more politicians.
